value: recommended=463 (NWNH committee appraisal, FY2010 $M over 2012 to 2021, to raise the astrophysics Explorer line from about 40 to about 100 $M per year by 2015, buying 2 MIDEX, 2 SMEX and 4 MoOs); delivered: AOs in 2014 (SMEX IXPE, MoO GUSTO), 2016 (MIDEX SPHEREx, MoO ARIEL/CASE), 2019 (SMEX, MoO) and 2021 (MIDEX, MoO), i.e. 2 SMEX, 2 MIDEX, 4 MoOs over 2012 to 2021 per Astro2020 Table H.1; Astro2020 finds NASA 'largely achieved' the 100 $M per year target; FY2022 Explorer request 300 (then-year $M, AIP); first AO 2014 versus a 2012 start, and the 2016 midterm found the first-half-decade support 'minimal' and the plan short of the full augmentation
rationale: Partial: the money and the mission count arrived, but late. No single delivered-dollar total for 2012 to 2021 was found on a reachable host; the FY2022 $300M request (AIP FY22 outlook) is the latest annual figure.

value: recommended=100-200 (NWNH committee appraisal, FY2010 $M over the decade, starting at about 4 $M per year with a possible late-decade ramp after a mid-decade review, to prepare a direct-imaging mission for a 2020-decade start); delivered: 2016 midterm Finding 4-11 says planned investment 'exceeds the level envisioned in NWNH', driven by the WFIRST coronagraph at 350 (FY2015 $M, within the WFIRST budget) plus starshade and coronagraph SAT work (SAT across all areas exceeded 64 $M in the first half of the decade); coronagraph tech-demo cost cap 334 (then-year $M, outside the 3200 development commitment, NASA KDP-C March 2020); ratio (coronagraph alone over recommended range)=1.7 to 3.3; timing: program ran through the decade, Roman Coronagraph launched 2026-08-30 with first observations as early as December 2026; the direct-imaging mission itself did not start in the 2020s (Astro2020 estimates about 600 FY2020 $M more technology work before Phase A)
rationale: Scored yes because the funding delivered exceeded the recommended $100M to $200M and the program ran on the recommended timeline: the 2016 midterm found the coronagraph plus starshade and SAT investment 'significantly exceeds' NWNH's level, the coronagraph later got a $334M cap (AIP FYI week of March 9 2020) and flew on Roman in August 2026. Marked guess because no source totals the decade's exoplanet technology spending and the coronagraph figure stands in for it, and because the end goal, a 2020-decade direct-imaging mission start, slipped (Astro2020 chapter 7 and Appendix I put the mission in the 2040s after about $600M more technology maturation).

value: recommended=60 (range 60-200; NWNH committee appraisal, FY2010 $M, mission-specific technology triggered only if B-modes were detected mid-decade, plus a 'modest' APRA augmentation for CMB technology); delivered: trigger never met (no primordial B-mode detection), so the 60 to 200 was never due; NASA funded CMB detector work through SAT (SAT across all areas exceeded 64 $M in the first half of the decade), the suborbital program rose by 7 $M per year to 32 $M per year in FY2013 to FY2015 (broadly the 15 $M per year NWNH asked for), and a LiteBIRD MoO Phase A study was funded from the 2014 Explorer AO (not selected; GUSTO was); ratio=not applicable (conditional spend not triggered); timing: on the NWNH schedule, with the decision point for a probe deferred by Astro2020 to a 2030s probe call
rationale: Scored yes because NWNH asked for a modest technology program with a $60M to $200M mission-specific effort only if B-modes were detected, the detection never came, and the 2016 midterm (Finding 4-12) found the program 'well aligned with the recommendations of NWNH' with NASA, NSF and DOE supporting technology development, balloons and precursor science; Astro2020 (nationalacademies.org/read/26141/chapter/9) then put a CMB probe as a candidate for a 2030s probe call rather than a 2020s start. Marked guess because no source gives the dollars NASA actually spent on CMB technology under this line, so delivery is judged from the midterm's qualitative finding and the suborbital and SAT figures.
